source_text: Et quia obtollendi in Ecclesiarum salutem tropaei damna perpetimur, quod bonae causae prudentia cognitorum miris erat delatura suffragiis; vel nihil aliud ad contumelias nostras vulgi valeret assensio. De his ergo, quas dixi, hominum partibus una nobis prodesset, altera nihil noceret, si aut illa potestatem obtineret, aut ista verecundiam. Verum quia rerum est magna confusio, et stolidorum maxima multitudo; eripiuntur Ecclesiae gubernacula rationis, ut erecto cornu velificet dogma populare.
pass_a_gloss: And because we suffer the losses of a trophy to be raised for the salvation of the Churches, which the prudence of knowers was going to confer on a good cause with remarkable votes; or at least the crowd's assent would avail nothing else toward our insults. Of these parts of men, therefore, which I have said, one would profit us, the other would harm nothing, if either that one obtained power, or this one shame. But because there is a great confusion of things, and a very great multitude of the dull; the steering-gear of reason is snatched from the Churches, so that a popular dogma may sail with horn raised.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: And since we suffer the loss of raising a trophy for the churches’ salvation—a trophy that discerning judges would have awarded our just cause with remarkable support—at least the crowd’s approval should have no further power to insult us. Of the two groups I have mentioned, one would then help us and the other do us no harm, if the first possessed authority or the second a sense of shame. But affairs are deeply confused, and fools are very numerous. The church is being robbed of reason’s steering gear so that popular doctrine can sail on with its horn held high.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
